text:
Die Gräfin Schlabrendorff wird mit die 50000 Rthl bis Weinachten
oder eigentlich bis d. 1ten Januar 1805 warten, zu einem längern
Termin hat sie Homuth nicht bewegen können.
Sie hat sehr kläglich gethan daß sie so viel verliere müste, und
Da sie keine Intressen von dieses Capital erhielte, so wäre der
Verlust noch größer wann sie langer als bis den 1 ten Januar
1805 warten solte -
Ist dem so daß Ewer durchlaucht bis dahin keine Interessen zahlen
dürfen, so glaube ich daß es leicht fallen wird, sich bey diesen
Termin zu beruhigen – Es sind doch dabey 2500 Rthl gewonnen –
und bis zu der Zeit wird Geld genug eingehen —
Homuth bittet um den Vergleich, damit er das nötige auf
sezzen und der Gräfin zur Vollziehung zu schicken könne –
Er wird probiren ob er bey der Gelegenheit die alten Wechsel
heraus bekommen kan.
Der Conducteur Cabanis ist abgegangen
Er wird sich draußen eine Bauer Fuhre
miethen die er glaubt vor 4 oder 5 Rthl.
zu erhalten. Hier wolte die Mieths
Kutscher 20 Rthl habe und verlangten
noch auf Entter und Gott weis was
eine Beihülfe —
v Triebenfeld
Breslau den 29ten Marz 1804.

translation.en:
Countess Schlabrendorff will wait for the 50000 Rthl until Christmas, or properly speaking until the 1st of January 1805; Homuth has not been able to move her to a longer term. She made a most piteous business of it, that she must lose so much, and since she received no interest on this capital the loss would be greater still were she to wait longer than until the 1st of January 1805. — If it be so that Your Serene Highness need pay no interest until then, I believe it will be an easy matter to rest content with this term. — There are, after all, 2500 Rthl gained thereby — and by that time money enough will come in. — Homuth asks for the settlement, so that he may draw up what is needful and send it to the Countess for execution. — He will try whether he can, on that occasion, get the old bills of exchange out of her hands.

The surveyor Cabanis has departed. Out there he will hire a peasant's conveyance, which he believes he can obtain for 4 or 5 Rthl. Here the hired coachmen wanted to have 20 Rthl and demanded besides an allowance for [uncertain: Entter] and God knows what

by way of assistance —

v Triebenfeld

Breslau, the 29th of March 1804.

text_english:
Countess Schlabrendorff will wait for the 50000 Rthl until Christmas, or properly speaking until the 1st of January 1805; Homuth has not been able to move her to a longer term. She made a most piteous business of it, that she must lose so much, and since she received no interest on this capital the loss would be greater still were she to wait longer than until the 1st of January 1805. — If it be so that Your Serene Highness need pay no interest until then, I believe it will be an easy matter to rest content with this term. — There are, after all, 2500 Rthl gained thereby — and by that time money enough will come in. — Homuth asks for the settlement, so that he may draw up what is needful and send it to the Countess for execution. — He will try whether he can, on that occasion, get the old bills of exchange out of her hands.

The surveyor Cabanis has departed. Out there he will hire a peasant's conveyance, which he believes he can obtain for 4 or 5 Rthl. Here the hired coachmen wanted to have 20 Rthl and demanded besides an allowance for [uncertain: Entter] and God knows what

by way of assistance —

v Triebenfeld

Breslau, the 29th of March 1804.
summary_en: Countess Schlabrendorff will wait for repayment of 50,000 Rthl until 1 January 1805 but no longer, Homuth having failed to obtain a longer term; she complains of her losses and of receiving no interest. If no interest is due until then, Triebenfeld advises accepting, since 2,500 Rthl is saved and money will have come in. Homuth wants the settlement drawn up for her signature and will try to recover her old bills of exchange. The surveyor Cabanis has set off, hiring a peasant's cart for 4 or 5 Rthl rather than a coachman at 20.
summary_de: Bericht über die Stundung der 50000 Rthl: Gräfin Schlabrendorff wartet nur bis Weihnachten, genauer bis zum 1. Januar 1805; Homuth konnte keine längere Frist erreichen, da sie keine Zinsen erhält und Verluste geltend macht. Triebenfeld rät zuzustimmen, weil bis dahin keine Zinsen fällig seien und so 2500 Rthl gewonnen würden; Homuth erbittet die Abrechnung für die Ausfertigung und will die alten Wechsel zurückerhalten. Der Landmesser Cabanis ist abgereist und nimmt vor Ort ein Bauernfuhrwerk für 4 bis 5 Rthl, da hiesige Kutscher 20 Rthl verlangten.
